The stdio path takes the raw JSON with no schema check, so if a server sends `"nextCursor": null` the loop keeps going (`null !== undefined`) and the next request goes out with `{ cursor: null }`. Depending on the server that either fails the whole listing or returns page one again and never stops. The SDK path doesn't hit this because its schema only accepts a string. Would narrowing it here be enough?

```suggestion
			cursor =
				typeof result.nextCursor === "string" ? result.nextCursor : undefined;
```

Also wondering if both loops should bail out when a server hands back the same cursor it was just sent, since right now that would spin until something else times out.
Fixed in 7d2aeef: stdio now accepts only string cursors, and both clients reject non-advancing cursors. Added three real-transport regressions; all 119 MCP tests pass.

Valid, fixed in the latest push. A Retry click carries no attachments of its own: protobuf decodes the omitted `images` field as `[]`, so `images ?? retry.images` kept the empty list. The retry now uses `images?.length ? images : retry.images`, so the failed start's attachments go to the retried sandbox unless the response actually carries some. Covered by `keeps the original attachments when Retry arrives with the webview's empty image list` in `SdkController.test.ts`, which sends Retry with `[]` and fails without the fix.

The same push merges `main` into this branch (the only conflict was in `state-keys.ts`, where `main` removed the focus-chain setting next to the new cloud keys). On the merged result, the full extension type check, vitest (1,452), `test:cloud` (23), the bun unit tests and the webview tests (584) all pass.
